questions.question: An article marked at ₹1,250 is sold at two successive discounts such that the selling price becomes ₹900. If the first discount is 20%, what is the second discount?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Price after **20% discount** = 1250 − 250 = ₹1,000 Final **Selling Price** = ₹900 Amount of second discount = 1000 − 900 = ₹100 Second **Discount percentage** = (100 ÷ 1000) × 100 = 10% **∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

questions.question: Find the mean proportional between (2 + sqrt{3}) and (10 - sqrt{75}) .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplify the second term: 10 − √75 = 10 − 5√3 = 5(2 − √3).

The numbers are (2 + √3) and 5(2 − √3).

Product = 5 × (2 + √3)(2 − √3) = 5 × (4 − 3) = 5.

Mean proportional = √Product = √5.

**∴ The correct answer is √5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number (a) = 2 + √3

Second number (b) = 10 − √75

**Formula Used:**

The **mean proportional** between two numbers a and b is given by x = √(a × b).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/679e7e9257965a43daed38515b90f6c2f3d619fe3aa937c792609a5e9bdf546e.png] 

⇒ First, simplify b = 10 − √(25 × 3) = 10 − 5√3

⇒ Factor out 5: b = 5(2 − √3)

⇒ Now, x = √[(2 + √3) × 5(2 − √3)]

⇒ x = √[5 × (2 + √3)(2 − √3)]

⇒ Using algebraic **identity** (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²:

⇒ x = √[5 × (2² − (√3)²)]

⇒ x = √[5 × (4 − 3)]

⇒ x = √[5 × 1] = √5

**∴ The correct answer is √5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional of two numbers a and b is x if a:x = x:b, which results in the formula x = √(ab).

Third Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the third proportional c is such that a:b = b:c, given by c = b²/a.

Conjugate Surds

Surds of the form (p + √q) and (p − √q) are conjugates; their product is always a rational number (p² − q).

questions.question: A cylindrical tank has a diameter of 12 m and a height of 10 m. If the tank is closed at both ends, what is the ratio of its curved surface area to its total surface area?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any **closed cylinder**, the ratio of **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** to **Total Surface Area (TSA)** is always h : (r + h).

Given **Height (h)** = 10 m and **Radius (r)** = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m.

Required Ratio = 10 : (6 + 10) = 10 : 16 = 5 : 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 5:8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given values for the **cylindrical tank**:

⇒ **Diameter** = 12 m

⇒ **Height (h)** = 10 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52e26f30d3121e9298f3b4e9f68a1c1e8d286dae2aaa1aece8c33c5175d7fa42.png] 

⇒ **Radius (r)** = **Diameter** ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m

⇒ **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 2 × π × r × h

⇒ **Total Surface Area (TSA)** = 2 × π × r × (r + h)

⇒ **Ratio** = [2 × π × r × h] ÷ [2 × π × r × (r + h)]

⇒ **Ratio** = h ÷ (r + h)

⇒ **Ratio** = 10 ÷ (6 + 10) = 10 ÷ 16

⇒ **Ratio** = 5 : 8

**∴ The correct answer is 5:8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cylinder

The total space occupied by a cylinder is given by V = πr²h.

Base Area of a Cylinder

The area of each circular end of the cylinder is πr².

Surface Area for Open Tanks

If a cylindrical tank is open at the top, its total surface area is 2πrh + πr².

questions.question: A tank is filled by two pipes, A and B, and emptied by a third pipe C. Pipe A fills the tank in 10 hours and pipe B in 15 hours. Pipe C empties it in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, and pipe C is closed after 4 hours, how much total time will it take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Capacity** of the tank = LCM(10, 15, 20) = 60 units.

Net efficiency of (A + B + C) = 6 + 4 − 3 = 7 units/hr.

Work done in 4 hours = 7 × 4 = 28 units.

**Remaining work** = 60 − 28 = 32 units.

Time for A and B to fill remaining = 32 ÷ (6 + 4) = 3.2 hr.

**Total Time** = 4 + 3.2 = 7.2 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.2 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Pipe A** fills in 10 hr, **Pipe B** fills in 15 hr, and **Pipe C** empties in 20 hr.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Net Efficiency × Time

⇒ Net efficiency of all three pipes (A + B − C) = 6 + 4 − 3 = 7 units/hr.

⇒ Work completed in the first **4 hours** = 7 × 4 = 28 units.

⇒ **Remaining work** to be completed after closing Pipe C = 60 − 28 = 32 units.

⇒ Efficiency of remaining pipes (A + B) = 6 + 4 = 10 units/hr.

⇒ Time taken to fill the remaining part = 32 ÷ 10 = 3.2 hr.

⇒ **Total time** required = Initial time + Remaining time = 4 hr + 3.2 hr = 7.2 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.2 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An **Inlet pipe** fills the tank (positive work), while an **Outlet pipe** empties the tank (negative work).

Net Efficiency

If multiple pipes operate simultaneously, the **Net Efficiency** is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies: Net Eff = EffIₙₗₑₜ₁ + EffIₙₗₑₜ₂ − EffOᵤₜₗₑₜ.

Time and Work Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the **Time** taken to complete the work (Efficiency = 1 ÷ Time), assuming the work is constant.

questions.question: A train overtakes two runners moving in the same direction at speeds of 5 km/h and 7 km/h, passing them completely in 18 seconds and 20 seconds, respectively. What is the length of the train (in metres)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Length of train** = (Difference in speeds × 5/18) × (t₁ × t₂) ÷ (t₂ − t₁)

Difference in speeds = 7 − 5 = 2 km/h

Length = (2 × 5/18) × (18 × 20) ÷ (20 − 18)

Length = (5/9) × 360 ÷ 2 = 5 × 20 = 100 m

**∴ The correct answer is 100 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Speed of runner₁ = 5 km/h, Speed of runner₂ = 7 km/h, Time taken t₁ = 18 s, t₂ = 20 s.

**Formula:** **Relative Speed** (same direction) = Speed of train − Speed of object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4a12f2cc0bd2e24ec99c44283c9973d846e08ac6ebbddb52c86e131a242a8cd2.png] 

Let **Speed of the train** be V km/h.

⇒ **Relative Speed** with first runner = (V − 5) × 5/18 m/s

⇒ **Relative Speed** with second runner = (V − 7) × 5/18 m/s

⇒ Length L = (V − 5) × (5/18) × 18 = (V − 7) × (5/18) × 20

⇒ (V − 5) × 1 = (V − 7) × (20/18)

⇒ 18(V − 5) = 20(V − 7)

⇒ 18V − 90 = 20V − 140

⇒ 2V = 50 ⇒ V = 25 km/h

⇒ L = (25 − 5) × (5/18) × 18 = 20 × 5 = 100 m

**∴ The correct answer is 100 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the **relative speed** is the difference between their speeds: (u − v).

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, the **relative speed** is the sum of their speeds: (u + v).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Length of Train

When a train passes a point object (man, pole, runner), the **distance covered** equals the **length of the train**.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells two types of pens, A and B. The total number of pens sold in a day is 120. The price of pen A is ₹12 each and pen B is ₹8 each. If the total sale amount is ₹1120, how many pens of type A did he sell?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume all **120 pens** are of **Type B** (₹8 each): Total sale = 120 × 8 = ₹960.

Actual total sale is **₹1120**, so the difference is 1120 − 960 = **₹160**.

Difference in price per pen between **Type A** and **Type B** = 12 − 8 = ₹4.

Number of **Type A pens** = 160 ÷ 4 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 pens.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total pens = 120 | Price of **Type A** = ₹12 | Price of **Type B** = ₹8 | Total Amount = ₹1120

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average Total = (n₁ × Price₁) + (n₂ × Price₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8dd3b67add298c5af80c6606c3170370967357ea2e3f0916568b4b2e4f753f16.png] 

Let the number of **Type A pens** be x and **Type B pens** be (120 − x).

⇒ 12 × x + 8 × (120 − x) = 1120

⇒ 12x + 960 − 8x = 1120

⇒ 4x + 960 = 1120

⇒ 4x = 1120 − 960

⇒ 4x = 160

⇒ x = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40 pens.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It is a rule that enables us to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at their respective prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a specified price.

Linear Equation Method

Standard method where unknown quantities are represented as variables (x, y) and solved using algebraic manipulation.

Weighted Average

The average of a data set that contains values with different levels of importance or frequency: Average = (Sum of all values) ÷ (Total number of items).

questions.question: Evaluate 22³ + (-18)³ + (-4)³
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the sum of the base numbers: 22 + (−18) + (−4) = 0.

When the **sum of three numbers is zero**, the sum of their cubes is **3 × Product of the numbers**.

Required value = 3 × 22 × (−18) × (−4) = 66 × 72 = 4752.

**∴ The correct answer is 4752.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The expression to evaluate is 22³ + (−18)³ + (−4)³.

Let **a = 22**, **b = −18**, and **c = −4**.

**Formula Used:**

We use the **algebraic identity**: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, calculate the sum of the variables: a + b + c = 22 + (−18) + (−4)

⇒ a + b + c = 22 − 22 = 0

⇒ Since **a + b + c = 0**, the identity simplifies to: a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

⇒ Substituting the values: 22³ + (−18)³ + (−4)³ = 3 × 22 × (−18) × (−4)

⇒ Value = 66 × 72

⇒ Value = 4752

Therefore, the correct option is 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 4752.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cubic Identity Properties

The expression a³ + b³ + c³ is equal to 3abc only if **a + b + c = 0** or if **a = b = c**. This is a fundamental **conditional identity** in algebra.

General Expansion

For any three numbers, a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = ½ (a + b + c)[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²].

Applications in Exams

This identity is frequently used to simplify large **cubic calculations** by checking if the sum of the bases equals zero before performing traditional multiplication.

questions.question: The mean proportional between 12 and a number is twice the mean proportional between 9 and 16. Find the number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Mean proportional** of 9 and 16 = √(9 × 16) = 12.

Given **mean proportional** of 12 and the number is **twice** this value.

Target MP = 2 × 12 = 24.

Using the property (MP)² = Product of numbers ⇒ 24² = 12 × Number.

Number = 576 ÷ 12 = 48.

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First set of numbers = 9 and 16

Second set of numbers = 12 and **x** (let the number be **x**)

**Formula Used:**

Mean proportional (MP) between two numbers **a** and **b** is √(a × b).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5fa878290c28226d2b5d7a16421807e041defe460f1279758ae4f42384adcbc1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mean proportional between 9 and 16 = √(9 × 16)

⇒ Mean proportional₍₉,₁₆₎ = √144 = 12

⇒ According to the question, MP₍₁₂,ₓ₎ = 2 × 12 = 24

⇒ √(12 × x) = 24

⇒ Squaring both sides: 12 × x = 24²

⇒ 12 × x = 576

⇒ x = 576 ÷ 12

⇒ x = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is √(a × b). If **x** is the mean proportional, then a : x :: x : b.

Third Proportional

For two numbers **a** and **b**, the third proportional **c** is such that a : b :: b : c, which gives c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers **a**, **b**, and **c**, the fourth proportional **d** is such that a : b :: c : d, giving d = (b × c) ÷ a.

questions.question: The largest four-digit number which when divided by 10, 11 and 8 leaves remainder 7 in each case is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Step 1: Calculate the **LCM** of 10, 11, and 8 ⇒ 440.

Step 2: Find the **largest 4-digit multiple** of 440 ⇒ 440 × 22 = 9680.

Step 3: Add the required **remainder** (7) to this multiple ⇒ 9680 + 7 = 9687.

**∴ The correct answer is 9687.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisors are 10, 11, and 8; **Remainder** in each case is 7.

**Formula Used:** Required Number = (LCM of divisors × k) + Remainder

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32e826ae3c7f113da35304f1ea0135724495585ebb254a56ae46bb6db9971d3d.png] 

⇒ **LCM**(10, 11, 8) = 2³ × 5 × 11 = 8 × 5 × 11 = 440

⇒ The **largest four-digit number** is 9999.

⇒ Dividing 9999 by 440: 9999 ÷ 440 = 22 with a remainder of 319.

⇒ The **largest multiple** of 440 below 10000 = 9999 − 319 = 9680.

⇒ The **required number** = 9680 + 7 = 9687.

**∴ The correct answer is 9687.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

It is the **smallest positive integer** that is evenly divisible by all numbers in a given set.

The Remainder Property

If a number N leaves a **constant remainder** R when divided by a, b, and c, then N = LCM(a, b, c) × k + R.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the **difference** between the sum of digits at odd places and even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question:
The average of 12 numbers is 38. If two more numbers 50 and 62 are included, the new average is

(Round off your answer to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total deviation from old average **38** = (**50** − 38) + (**62** − 38) = 12 + 24 = **36**.

Total numbers now = 12 + 2 = **14**.

Average increase = Total deviation ÷ Total count = 36 ÷ 14 ≈ **2.57**.

New Average = 38 + 2.57 = **40.57**.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.57.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of **12 numbers** = **38**, Included numbers = **50** and **62**.

**Formula:** New Average = (Old Sum + New Values) ÷ New Count

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6301af2498d024e0826c30239a1cabab94d719982a12d2fe642a64edf60514b8.png] 

⇒ Sum of 12 numbers = 12 × 38 = **456**

⇒ Sum of 14 numbers = 456 + 50 + 62 = **568**

⇒ Total count = 12 + 2 = **14**

⇒ New Average = 568 ÷ 14 = **40.5714...**

⇒ Rounding to two decimal places, New Average = **40.57**

**∴ The correct answer is 40.57.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Average Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).

Weighted Average

When two groups are combined, New Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Inclusion/Exclusion Rule

If the newly added value is **greater** than the current average, the new average will **increase**.

questions.question: X, Y, and Z enter into a partnership. X invests ₹60,000 for 12 months, Y invests ₹80,000 for 6 months, and Z invests ₹1,20,000 for 4 months. If the total profit is ₹77,000, what is the share of Z?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Ratio of Profit = (Capital × Time)X : (Capital × Time)Y : (Capital × Time)Z Ratio = (60 × 12) : (80 × 6) : (120 × 4) = 720 : 480 : 480 Simplified Ratio = 3 : 2 : 2 Total units = 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 units → ₹77,000 Z's share (2 units) = (77,000 ÷ 7) × 2 = ₹22,000 **∴ The correct answer is ₹22,000.**

questions.question: A shirt originally costing ₹800 is first decreased by 30% and then increased by 15%. What is its new price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change formula: **Net % = a + b + (ab/100)**

Here, a = −30 (decrease) and b = +15 (increase).

Net change = −30 + 15 + [(−30 × 15) / 100] = −15 − 4.5 = **−19.5%**.

New Price = 800 − (19.5% of 800) = 800 − 156 = **644**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹644.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Original Price of the **shirt** = ₹800, First change = 30% decrease, Second change = 15% increase.

**Method:** Step-by-step price calculation using basic percentage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fcb41e14724ec831a056cd35863ad5f7e2c99c050202a22e65960a7c772eabb9.png] 

⇒ Price after 30% decrease = Original Price × [ (100 − 30) / 100 ]

⇒ Intermediate Price = 800 × (70 / 100) = ₹560

⇒ Final price after 15% increase = Intermediate Price × [ (100 + 15) / 100 ]

⇒ New Price = 560 × (115 / 100) = 5.6 × 115 = ₹644

Thus, the final price of the **shirt** is **₹644**, which corresponds to **Option (4)**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹644.**

questions.question: Nitin sells two articles for ₹2,973 each with no profit, no loss in the entire transaction. If one article was sold at a gain of 50%, then the other article is sold at a loss of:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Gain** of 50% = 1/2 ⇒ Ratio of CP : SP for **Article 1** = 2 : 3.

Since **Selling Price** is the same for both, SP of **Article 2** = 3 units.

**No profit, no loss** condition implies: **Profit** on Article 1 = **Loss** on Article 2.

Profit on Article 1 = 3 − 2 = 1 unit. So, Loss on Article 2 = 1 unit.

CP of Article 2 = SP + Loss = 3 + 1 = 4 units.

**Loss %** on Article 2 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of **Article 1** = **₹2,973**

Selling Price (SP) of **Article 2** = **₹2,973**

**Gain %** on Article 1 = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Gain%)

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9969b98e992cdcc1e134f6228e62fb44277c57025807ead5b258816e29eec5a1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **CP of Article 1** = (2973 × 100) ÷ (100 + 50)

⇒ CP₁ = (2973 × 100) ÷ 150 = **₹1,982**

⇒ **Profit on Article 1** = 2973 − 1982 = **₹991**

⇒ Since overall there is **no profit, no loss**:

⇒ Loss on Article 2 = Profit on Article 1 = **₹991**

⇒ **CP of Article 2** = SP of Article 2 + Loss

⇒ CP₂ = 2973 + 991 = **₹3,964**

⇒ **Loss % on Article 2** = (991 ÷ 3964) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 1/4 × 100 = **25%**

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

No Profit, No Loss Condition

This occurs when the total **Cost Price** of all articles equals the total **Selling Price**. Mathematically, Total CP = Total SP, or Profit from one item = Loss from another.

Cost Price with Gain/Loss

When gain is given, CP = SP × 100 / (100 + Gain%). When loss is given, CP = SP × 100 / (100 − Loss%).

Successive Changes

If an article's price is changed successively by x% and y%, the net change is given by the formula: [x + y + (xy ÷ 100)]%.

questions.question: The measure of an interior angle of a regular polygon is 162°. Find the number of sides of the polygon.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **regular polygon**, the sum of an **interior angle** and an **exterior angle** at any vertex is always 180°.

⇒ **Exterior angle** = 180° − **Interior angle** = 180° − 162° = 18°.

The **number of sides (n)** of a regular polygon is given by 360° ÷ **exterior angle**.

⇒ n = 360° ÷ 18° = 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 sides.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Measure of each **interior angle** = 162°

**Formula Used:**

Each **interior angle** of a **regular polygon** with **n sides** = [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d754721016b8dd14373000fe046411acc09d9ff2ab6bd3e9ffa493e204c83fca.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 162° = [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n

⇒ 162n = (n − 2) × 180

⇒ 162n = 180n − 360

⇒ 180n − 162n = 360

⇒ 18n = 360

⇒ n = 360 ÷ 18

⇒ n = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 sides.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The total sum of all **interior angles** of a polygon with **n sides** is always (n − 2) × 180°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

For any convex polygon, the sum of all **exterior angles** (one at each vertex) is exactly 360°.

Regular Polygon Properties

In a **regular polygon**, all **sides** are equal and all **interior angles** are equal. Each exterior angle = 360° ÷ n.

questions.question: From the top of a cliff 80 meters high, the angles of depression of two ships in the same direction are 30° and 60°. Find the distance between the ships (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The distance **d** between two objects in the **same direction** from a **cliff** of height **h** is given by: **d = h × (cot θ₁ − cot θ₂)**.

Given: **h = 80 m**, **θ₁ = 30°**, and **θ₂ = 60°**.

d = 80 × (cot 30° − cot 60°) = 80 × (√3 − 1/√3) = 80 × (2/√3).

d = 160 / 1.732 ≈ **92.38 m**.

**∴ The correct answer is 92.38 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Height of the **cliff (AB)** = **80 m**. **Angles of depression** of **ships C and D** are **60°** and **30°** respectively.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/34d48819635517eb6dcb566f56242a62ec9512f49af90f77f136a127e0242065.png] 

In right-angled triangle **ABC**:

⇒ tan 60° = AB / BC

⇒ √3 = 80 / BC

⇒ BC = 80 / √3 m

In right-angled triangle **ABD**:

⇒ tan 30° = AB / BD

⇒ 1 / √3 = 80 / BD

⇒ BD = 80√3 m

**Distance between ships (CD)** = BD − BC:

⇒ CD = 80√3 − 80 / √3

⇒ CD = (80 × 3 − 80) / √3 = 160 / √3

⇒ CD = 160 / 1.73205 ≈ **92.376 m**

Rounding off to two decimal places, we get **92.38 m**.

**∴ The correct answer is 92.38 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression

The angle formed between the **horizontal line** and the line of sight when an observer looks **downward** at an object.

Distance for Opposite Sides

If ships are on **opposite sides** of the cliff, the distance between them is **d = h(cot α + cot β)**.

Trigonometric Identities

For calculations, remember **tan 30° = 1/√3**, **tan 60° = √3**, and **√3 ≈ 1.732**.

questions.question: A delivery rider travels from Warehouse A to Store B, a distance of 48 km, at a speed of 32 km/hr. On the return journey along the same route, due to traffic, he travels at a speed of 24 km/hr. What is the rider’s average speed for the entire trip? (Round off up to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the **distance** is the same for both ways (48 km), we use the **Harmonic Mean** formula for **average speed**.

Average Speed = (2 × s₁ × s₂) / (s₁ + s₂)

Average Speed = (2 × 32 × 24) / (32 + 24) = (2 × 32 × 24) / 56

Average Speed = (32 × 24) / 28 = (8 × 24) / 7 = 192 / 7 ≈ 27.43 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 27.43 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance from **Warehouse A** to **Store B** = 48 km

Speed during onward journey (s₁) = 32 km/hr

Speed during return journey (s₂) = 24 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf4ef921bfa1f63be034aa171209d8e2af6a44bb15bdf841b06d6399615317a7.png] 

⇒ Total Distance = 48 + 48 = 96 km

⇒ Time taken for onward journey (t₁) = Distance ÷ s₁ = 48 ÷ 32 = 1.5 hours

⇒ Time taken for return journey (t₂) = Distance ÷ s₂ = 48 ÷ 24 = 2 hours

⇒ Total Time = t₁ + t₂ = 1.5 + 2 = 3.5 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 96 ÷ 3.5

⇒ Average Speed = 960 ÷ 35 = 192 ÷ 7 ≈ 27.4285...

**∴ The correct answer is 27.43 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Fixed Distance)

When an object covers equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (Fixed Time)

When an object travels for the same duration at speeds x and y, the average speed is the arithmetic mean: (x + y) ÷ 2.

General Average Speed

For any journey, Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂ + ... + dₙ) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + ... + tₙ).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: The original price of a refrigerator was $1,500. During a clearance sale, it was initially discounted by 30%, followed by an additional 10% discount on the reduced price. What is the total percentage discount applied to the refrigerator?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Successive Discount** formula: **a + b − (a × b)/100**.

Given: **a = 30%** and **b = 10%**.

Net Discount % = 30 + 10 − (30 × 10)/100

Net Discount % = 40 − 3 = 37%

**∴ The correct answer is 37%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Original Price = **1,500**, First Discount = **30%**, Second Discount = **10%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82ae59ffda7842e45ef5014b695abcb559d1c741648d1e28f8a0f90af896ae7a.png] 

⇒ First discount amount = 30% of 1,500 = (30/100) × 1500 = 450

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 1500 − 450 = 1050

⇒ Second discount amount = 10% of 1,050 = (10/100) × 1050 = 105

⇒ Final Selling Price = 1050 − 105 = 945

⇒ Total Discount = 1500 − 945 = 555

⇒ Equivalent Discount % = (Total Discount / Original Price) × 100

⇒ Equivalent Discount % = (555 / 1500) × 100 = 37%

**∴ The correct answer is 37%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Discount for Three Rates

For three successive discounts a%, b%, and c%, the net discount is calculated by first finding the net of a and b, then applying the formula to that result and c.

Marked Price (MP) and Selling Price (SP)

Discount is always computed on the **Marked Price**. SP = MP × (100 − D₁%)/100 × (100 − D₂%)/100.

Multiplying Factor Method

Final Price = Initial Price × 0.70 × 0.90. The overall multiplier is 0.63, which implies a (1 − 0.63) × 100 = 37% discount.

Amount Calculation

Time and Rate Relationship

Constant Annual Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest earned remains the same for each year of the time period.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks the price of sugar 24% above the cost price and gives a discount of 18%, but uses a weight of 800 grams instead of 1 kg. Find his overall profit percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **overall profit** is the product of individual multipliers for **markup**, **discount**, and **weight fraud**.

Net Multiplier = (1 + 24/100) × (1 − 18/100) × (1000 ÷ 800)

Net Multiplier = 1.24 × 0.82 × 1.25

Net Multiplier = 1.0168 × 1.25 = 1.271

Profit % = (1.271 − 1) × 100 = 27.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 27.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Markup = **24%** above CP | Discount = **18%** | Actual weight = **800 g** | Declared weight = **1 kg** (1000 g).

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 1240 − 18% of 1240 = 1240 − 223.2 = ₹1016.8.

⇒ Since the shopkeeper gives only **800 g**, his **actual CP** = ₹800.

⇒ Total **Profit** = SP − Actual CP = 1016.8 − 800 = ₹216.8.

⇒ **Overall Profit %** = (216.8 ÷ 800) × 100 = 27.1%.

**∴ The correct answer is 27.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) for **Bank A** and **Bank B** = **₹2,60,000** each.

Interest Rate (R₁) for **Bank A** = 3.5% per annum.

Interest Rate (R₂) for **Bank B** = 6.5% per annum.

Time period (T) = **2 years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d6149fd5c0d81a9370ef36e4bee76dd564f9814a89fcb1814929327c9c0e87f8.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest (SI)** = (Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest paid to **Bank A** (SIA) = (2,60,000 × 3.5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SIA = 2,600 × 7 = 18,200

⇒ Interest paid to **Bank B** (SIB) = (2,60,000 × 6.5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SIB = 2,600 × 13 = 33,800

⇒ **Positive Difference** = SIB − SIA

⇒ Difference = 33,800 − 18,200 = 15,600

According to the calculation, the interest difference is ₹15,600 which corresponds to option (2).

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Principle

Simple interest is calculated only on the initial **Principal** amount. The formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is annual rate, and T is time in years.

Interest Difference Shortcut

When Principal and Time are constant, the difference in interest is directly proportional to the difference in rates: Difference = [P × T × (R₂ − R₁)] ÷ 100.

Total Amount

The total amount (A) to be repaid after the time period is the sum of the Principal and the Interest: A = P + SI.

questions.question:
The sides of a rectangular field are 55 m and 70 m long. Its area is equal to the area of a circular field. What is the perimeter (in m) of the circular field?

(Take π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Area of rectangular field** = 55 × 70 = 3850 m².

As per the problem, **Area of circular field** = πr² = 3850 m².

⇒ (22/7) × r² = 3850 ⇒ r² = 175 × 7 = 1225 ⇒ r = 35 m.

**Perimeter (Circumference)** = 2πr = 2 × (22/7) × 35 = 220 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 220 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the **rectangular field** (L) = 70 m

Breadth of the **rectangular field** (B) = 55 m

**Formula Used:**

Area of **rectangle** = Length × Breadth

Area of **circular field** = π × r²

Perimeter (**Circumference**) of circle = 2 × π × r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4ef041ac876b4c5e152812d21b478167eab30524d8f4ee75fd1eed1d383d3833.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Area of rectangular field** = 70 × 55 = 3850 m²

⇒ Area of **circular field** = 3850 m²

⇒ πr² = 3850

⇒ (22/7) × r² = 3850

⇒ r² = (3850 × 7) ÷ 22

⇒ r² = 175 × 7 = 1225

⇒ **Radius** (r) = √1225 = 35 m

⇒ **Perimeter** = 2 × (22/7) × 35

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × 22 × 5 = 220 m

**∴ The correct answer is 220 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circle Properties

The ratio of the **circumference** to the **diameter** of any circle is always constant, denoted by π (≈ 22/7 or 3.14).

Comparison of Perimeter

For a given area, a **circle** has the shortest perimeter compared to any other plane figure like a rectangle or square.

Unit Conversion

Ensure all dimensions are in the same units (e.g., meters) before equating areas or calculating perimeters.
